title: LIBERO Robotic Arm Control Visual Evidence
subtitle: Real simulator rollout videos from the work4 OpenVLA-OFT visual-capture run on LIBERO-10.

teaser.caption: Actual LIBERO simulator rollout captured from N263B. The task is to put the alphabet soup and tomato sauce in the basket. This is qualitative control footage, not a metric animation.

abstract: This page now foregrounds the visible robotic control behavior instead of a reproduction scoreboard. The videos show OpenVLA-OFT controlling a simulated tabletop manipulation task in LIBERO-10 through the local work4 evaluation harness.

The two episodes are failure cases, but they are useful visual evidence because they expose what the controller actually does in the scene. The page therefore presents them as qualitative rollout footage and keeps metric interpretation out of the first screen.

method.title: Visual Capture Protocol
points: Task: put both the alphabet soup and the tomato sauce in the basket.
Suite: LIBERO-10 task 0 with two recorded episodes and seed 7.
Recording: 20 FPS videos with 221 frames per episode from the actual simulator rollout.
Repair: the harness video recorder was patched for Python 3.8 type-alias compatibility before rerun.

timeline.event: Initial N263 visual capture reached the model server but failed before rollout because the harness video module used an incompatible runtime type alias.
N263B started after adding a video-recorder compatibility patch and import check.
N263B completed two LIBERO-10 task-0 episodes and exported two MP4 rollout videos, each with 221 frames.

boundaries: The videos are real simulator rollouts, not generated illustrations and not metric animations.
Both displayed episodes are failure cases, so the page should be read as qualitative control evidence rather than a success demonstration.
This is not hardware robot evidence and does not support a sim-to-real claim.
The broader public-baseline metric table remains an evidence snapshot, but it is not the main homepage content.
next_actions: Capture one or more successful-looking qualitative rollouts if a later policy or task produces them.
Add side-by-side videos only when the media comes from real recorded episodes.
Keep the data table as secondary evidence and use the homepage primarily for intuitive control behavior.
